headline: Sterling opened the week steady at about 1.333 dollars, near Friday's close and the top of last week's range. The dollar is near its softest this month as traders see little chance of a Fed rise on 28 October, while unrest in France and a slight fall in oil are the weekend's news.

drivers.title: Fed rate expectations
drivers.text: The Fed's range is 3.75% to 4% after its September rise. On Monday 19 October fed funds futures put the chance of a hold at the 28 October meeting at about 84%, little changed from Friday, Reuters reported, citing the CME FedWatch tool. The Fed is in its quiet period, so no official will comment before the decision.

drivers.title: US bond yields
drivers.text: The US ten-year yield fell to about 5.11% on Thursday 15 October, a three-week low, from about 5.33% on Wednesday, and edged up to about 5.12% on Friday, Trading Economics reported. Higher US yields draw money into the dollar and lower ones do the reverse; the dollar index was 101.83 in Asian trade on Monday.

drivers.title: Oil and the Gulf
drivers.text: Brent touched $110 (about £83) a barrel on Friday 16 October for the first time since May, as attacks on shipping cut Gulf crude flows to about 8.5 million barrels a day last week from more than 20 million the week before, Kpler said. It slipped to about $108.43 (about £81) early on Monday after the US waiver on Russian sanctions. Dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: Bank Rate is 3.75% and markets have priced a Bank of England rise on 5 November. On Friday 16 October Governor Bailey said the knock-on effects of energy prices on UK inflation look subdued so far, a softer tone than in late September. This week's pay and inflation figures are the last big UK data before that meeting, and investors remain cautious ahead of the Budget later this month.

drivers.title: Europe
drivers.text: Violent cost of living protests in France pushed the euro down 0.1% to $1.1225 early on Monday, Reuters reported, with the effect coming mainly through French government bonds. A weaker euro steadies the dollar index. The European Central Bank meets on 29 October, the day after the Fed.

lower: UK pay growth or inflation coming in below forecast this week, which would put the expected Bank of England rise on 5 November in doubt and weigh on the pound.
More attacks on Gulf shipping or Saudi oil sites pushing oil back above $110 (about £83), which would tend to lift the dollar.
Deeper unrest in France unsettling European bond markets, which would weaken the euro and strengthen the dollar index.
Renewed worries about tax rises in the Budget later this month, which would weigh on the pound.
higher: UK inflation on Wednesday at or above the 3.4% forecast, which would support a Bank of England rise on 5 November and lift the pound.
More Russian fuel reaching the market or progress on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which would bring oil down, ease US inflation worries and weaken the dollar.
Markets becoming surer that the Fed will hold on 28 October, which would keep US yields and the dollar soft.
watch: UK pay figures come out at 10:00 Dubai on Tuesday 20 October, with average earnings growth forecast at 3.8% against 3.9% last time. UK inflation for September follows at 10:00 Dubai on Wednesday 21 October, forecast at 3.4% against 3.1%, and Governor Bailey speaks at 17:00 Dubai that day. Figures above forecast would support the Bank of England rise expected on 5 November and help someone selling pounds for dirhams, while figures below would weigh on the pound. UK retail sales and the UK and US business surveys follow on Friday 23 October.

feed.title: Sterling has reopened steady after a quiet weekend
feed.text: The banks' market reopened at 01:00 Dubai with GBP/USD dipping from 1.3322, Kraken's last weekend price, to about 1.3303 within 15 minutes, as EUR/USD fell by a similar share in thin opening trade. Both recovered within the hour, and GBP/USD was back near 1.3333 by 02:25 Dubai and 1.3328 at 07:30 Dubai, close to Friday's close. Reuters reported the pound flat at $1.3329 in early Asian trade, with the dollar index level at 101.83 and traders still putting the chance of no Fed change on 28 October at about 84%.

feed.title: Violent protests in France have weighed on the euro, steadying the dollar
feed.text: President Macron condemned violence at cost of living protests in a televised address on Sunday, after one of France's worst days of unrest in years, and the euro fell 0.1% to $1.1225 as Asian trading began, Reuters reported. The euro is the largest part of the dollar index, so its fall kept the dollar from slipping further, which holds back GBP/USD. The pound itself was unmoved, so dirhams per pound were little changed.

feed.title: Oil has eased after a US waiver on Russian sanctions
feed.text: Brent fell about 1.3% to $108.43 (about £81) a barrel by 00:40 Dubai, after President Trump signed an order on Friday waiving sanctions and tariffs on Russia that may allow more Russian fuel exports, Reuters reported; Brent had settled on Friday at its highest since 19 May. Cheaper oil eases US inflation worries and tends to weaken the dollar, but GBP/USD showed no clear reaction this morning.

feed.title: Governor Bailey's Saturday talk was about AI, not interest rates
feed.text: At the G30 banking seminar in Bangkok on Saturday, Governor Bailey spoke about AI and financial stability, including the risk of a market correction if investors rethink AI's short-term gains, and said nothing about UK interest rates, The Nation reported. He gave no new signal on the Bank of England's 5 November decision, where markets expect a rise. Kraken's weekend price, a guide to the reopening, held between 1.3323 and 1.3336 through his talk and was 1.3322 early on Sunday, against 1.3329 at Friday's close.

feed.title: The dollar has slipped back as the week closes
feed.text: GBP/USD edged up from 1.3317 at 22:45 Dubai to about 1.3328 at 23:39, recovering part of the early evening dip. EUR/USD rose a little, from 1.1230 to 1.1234, and the pound gained slightly on the euro, so this was a softer dollar with a slightly firmer pound in thin late Friday trade. Trading Economics reported the dollar index at about 101.6 on Friday, its lowest in two weeks and down about 0.4% on the week, with markets putting the chance of no Fed change in October at about 85%; no single report explains this last hour.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed into the weekend
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from 1.3343 at 19:40 Dubai to about 1.3316 at 20:39, and EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from 1.1244 to 1.1213, while the pound held steady against the euro, so this was the dollar gaining across the board rather than the pound weakening. No UK or US figure was due in that hour; Trading Economics reported the US ten-year yield edging up to about 5.12% on Friday after Thursday's sharp fall, which makes holding dollars a little more rewarding, but no report read so far explains this particular move. Reports still describe the dollar as set for its first weekly fall in about a month.

feed.title: Sterling has eased back from this week's high
feed.text: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3372 at 18:30 Dubai to 1.3342 at 19:39, giving back most of the afternoon's climb. The pound also lost ground to the euro, with EUR/GBP up from 0.8420 to about 0.8430, while EUR/USD dipped only from 1.1254 to 1.1244, so this was mainly the pound easing rather than fresh dollar strength. No UK or US figure was due in that hour and no report read so far explains the move.

feed.title: Sterling has climbed again as US trading opens
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from 1.3336 at 17:29 Dubai to about 1.3372 by 18:30, its highest this week, and was near 1.3365 at 18:40 Dubai. The rise was partly a weaker dollar and partly a firmer pound, with EUR/USD up from 1.1241 to 1.1253 and the euro down against the pound from 0.8429 to 0.8420. US industrial production, out at 17:15 Dubai, rose 0.7% in September after 0.1% in August, a firm figure that would normally help the dollar, and no report read so far explains this latest leg beyond the dollar's slide since Chair Warsh's remarks this morning.

feed.title: Sterling has climbed to its highest this week as the dollar keeps falling
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from 1.3309 at 08:40 Dubai to about 1.3345 by 14:30, its highest since the market reopened on Monday. The dollar has kept sliding through the European morning since Fed Chair Warsh declined in Bangkok to say whether rates will rise in October or December, and his remarks pushed US bond yields lower again, which makes holding dollars less rewarding.

feed.title: Sterling has recovered about 1.5% since Wednesday's low
feed.text: The dollar hit an 18-month high on Wednesday after hot US inflation figures, taking GBP/USD down to about 1.3150. It turned on Thursday, when the Fed's Bowman and Daly said the Fed could wait for more clarity, investors worried about heavy debts in the AI sector, and UK output beat forecasts with growth of 0.1% in August against a 0.1% fall expected. Each pound now buys about 1.5% more dirhams than at Wednesday's low.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened as Chair Warsh declines to commit to another rise
feed.text: In his Bangkok conversation with IMF Managing Director Georgieva, Fed Chair Warsh said the Fed has made clear it will deliver price stability but that he does not believe in prejudging meetings, and that judgements will be made at the October and December meetings. This week's hot inflation figures had raised talk of a second rise in October, and the absence of a firmer signal weakened the dollar, with the dollar index down to about 101.80, its lowest in ten days, while the pound held steady against the euro; a weaker dollar means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from 1.3279 at 07:42 Dubai to 1.3303 at 07:50 and 1.3306 at 07:57, eased to near 1.3296 by 08:10 and was near 1.3309 at 08:39 Dubai.

feed.title: Chair Warsh has spoken in Bangkok with little market reaction so far
feed.text: Fed Chair Warsh began a conversation with IMF Managing Director Georgieva in Bangkok at 07:30 Dubai, his last scheduled remarks before the Fed's quiet period ahead of the 28 October meeting, but no report read so far carries what he said. A firm line on inflation would make another Fed rise more likely and lift the dollar, and a cautious one would do the reverse. In the first ten minutes there was no sign of either: GBP/USD went from 1.3285 at 07:29 Dubai to 1.3284 at 07:30 and was near 1.3282 at 07:39 Dubai.

feed.title: Governor Bailey has sounded measured on UK inflation
feed.text: Speaking in Bangkok at 06:00 Dubai, Governor Bailey said the wider effects of high energy prices on UK prices look subdued so far but it is too early to be sure, with businesses cutting costs rather than passing them on; he called above-target inflation enormously frustrating. That is softer than his warnings in late September, which takes a little support from the pound, though it leaves a November rise open. GBP/USD barely moved, edging from 1.3275 at 05:59 Dubai to 1.3280 at 06:01 and settling near 1.3277 by 06:10 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has won back some ground in the New York afternoon
feed.text: No report read so far names a trigger for this move, which reverses part of the dollar's retreat earlier in the New York morning; the reports read describe Thursday as a choppy day after hotter than expected US shop sales and producer prices. The dollar firmed across the board, with the euro falling against it from 1.1220 to 1.1205 while the pound held steady against the euro, so this was a dollar move and it means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD slipped from 1.3274 at 18:41 Dubai to 1.3253 by 18:56 and touched 1.3250 at 19:06, and was near 1.3256 at 19:39 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened again in the New York morning
feed.text: No report read so far names a trigger for this move, which began at 18:30 Dubai, an hour after the New York stock market opened, and looks like a resumption of the dollar's retreat from Wednesday's high as US bond yields stay near three-week lows. The dollar softened across the board, with the euro rising against it from 1.1209 to 1.1221 while the pound held steady against the euro, so this was a dollar move and it means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from 1.3260 at 18:29 Dubai to 1.3273 within five minutes and 1.3275 by 18:37, and was near 1.3273 at 18:39 Dubai.

feed.title: US shop sales and producer prices have come in hotter than expected
feed.text: US retail sales rose 0.8% in September against 0.3% forecast, and producer prices jumped 1.3% against 0.6% forecast, with the core measure up 0.5% against 0.3%. Strong spending and rising costs make a Fed rise more likely, which tends to lift US yields and the dollar, so fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD dipped from 1.3251 to 1.3236 within four minutes of the release, then recovered to about 1.3257 within ten minutes; no source read so far explains the quick recovery.

feed.title: The dollar has slipped further in late morning trade
feed.text: No report names a single trigger for this move, which looks like a continuation of the dollar's retreat from Wednesday's high as US bond yields stay near three-week lows ahead of this afternoon's US retail sales and producer prices. The dollar softened across the board, with the euro rising against it from 1.1211 to 1.1222 while the pound also edged up against the euro, so both sides helped and the result is more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from 1.3241 at 12:00 Dubai to 1.3269 by 12:30 and was near 1.3262 at 12:39 Dubai.

feed.title: Governor Bailey's slot has passed with no market reaction
feed.text: Bank of England Governor Bailey was listed to speak at 11:30 Dubai, during the IMF and World Bank meetings week in Bangkok, but no report so far carries any new remarks on interest rates; his reported comments in Bangkok on Wednesday were about fraud on social media platforms. With nothing new on rates, the pound had no fresh reason to move, and GBP/USD went from 1.3248 at 11:29 Dubai to 1.3247 at 11:30 and was near 1.3250 at 11:40 Dubai.

feed.title: The UK economy has grown when a fall was expected
feed.text: The ONS said the economy grew by 0.1% in August against a forecast fall of 0.1%, with factory output up 1.2% while services were flat and construction fell for a fourth month, and growth over the year reached 2.1% against 1.7% expected. Stronger UK figures support the Bank of England rise that markets already expect on 5 November, which lifts the pound, and the pound did firm against the euro from 0.8470 to 0.8464. Against the dollar the effect was small: GBP/USD briefly touched 1.3248 at 10:00 Dubai from 1.3238, settled near 1.3243 by 10:05 and was near 1.3233 at 10:38 Dubai as the dollar firmed slightly.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened as US bond yields have fallen back
feed.text: US government bonds recovered overnight from the sell-off that followed Wednesday's hot inflation figures, taking the ten-year yield to about 5.11%, a three-week low and about two tenths of a point below its post-inflation high, as a slide in technology shares sent money into bonds and an unconfirmed Bloomberg report suggested China is quietly holding more Treasuries through Canada. Lower US yields make the dollar less rewarding to hold, so it weakened across the board and the dollar index fell about 0.6% to about 102, which means more dirhams per pound; the pound itself eased slightly against the euro, so this was a dollar move. GBP/USD rose from 1.3190 at 02:00 Dubai to 1.3232 by 04:00, then from 1.3231 at 06:00 to 1.3250 within fifteen minutes, and was near 1.3253 at 07:39 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has eased back from its highs
feed.text: No report names a single trigger, but the dollar gave back part of the day's gains across the board: the euro rose against the dollar from 1.1116 to 1.1153 while barely moving against the pound, and Brent crude slipped back to about $106 (about £80) a barrel after the US said it had helped more than 19 million barrels through the Strait of Hormuz. The Fed's Beige Book at 22:00 Dubai found growth in nine of its twelve districts against ten in August and mostly flat consumer spending, though price pressures had broadened, and a slower US economy tends to weaken the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from a low of 1.3138 at 20:15 Dubai to 1.3169 by the Beige Book and to about 1.3186 by 22:37 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped further in the London afternoon
feed.text: No report names a fresh trigger for the fall between 18:47 and 19:12 Dubai, and the US ten-year yield and Brent crude were both a little below their earlier highs. This time the pound weakened as well as the dollar strengthening: the euro fell against the dollar from 1.1125 to 1.1112 while it rose against the pound from 0.8446 to 0.8453, so both sides meant fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD fell from 1.3169 at 18:47 Dubai to a low of 1.3138 at 19:12, its weakest since late June, then steadied near 1.3146 by 19:38 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has extended its gains into the US afternoon
feed.text: No report names a fresh trigger for the slide between 17:47 and 18:02 Dubai; it was a broad rise in the dollar, with the euro falling at the same time from 1.1128 to 1.1116, as the dollar index reached about 102.9, its highest since April 2025, and US shares fell after the open, Trading Economics reported. A stronger dollar means fewer dirhams per pound, and markets still put the chance of a Fed rise this month at about 50% after the hotter inflation figures. GBP/USD fell from 1.3193 at 17:47 Dubai to a low of 1.3163 at 18:02, the weakest since June, then steadied near 1.3173 by 18:38 Dubai.

feed.title: US yields have jumped and the dollar has kept climbing
feed.text: The US ten-year yield rose about nine hundredths of a point to about 5.31% after the hotter inflation figures, close to highs last seen in early 2002, and markets now put the chance of a Fed rise this month at about 50%, up from about 22% before the release, Trading Economics reported. Higher US yields and a likelier Fed rise draw money into the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound, and the dollar index reached about 102.7, its highest since April 2025. GBP/USD slid further from 1.3214 at 16:40 Dubai to a low of about 1.3187 at 17:20, then steadied near 1.3200 by 17:38 Dubai.
